\begin{abstract}
Web applications enforce authorization on the server, yet their interfaces can
still show what a role should not see or omit what a policy requires. We
present \sys{}, a prototype that explores an application as one fixed role and
checks each reached state against a role-scoped policy of forbidden and required
elements, computed as an intersection and a set difference over a semantic state description. The evaluation is fixture-level: one six-page
application with four planted violations and seven small same-project apps,
using fakes. Under oracle perception the production audit agrees
with the ground truth, a consistency check. A
rule-based channel fails mainly by vocabulary mismatch; an in-sample label script
beats it on the first app but finds 3 of 8 forbidden violations on four generated
apps; and a simulated crash shows that claim-before-execute does not by
itself make resumption safe. No browser or VLM pipeline is evaluated.
\keywords{web UI testing, test oracles, negation, vision-language models,
state-space exploration}
\end{abstract}
